project_id: Big League Smart Contract Audit Report - QuillAudits

preconditions.description: Victim (token holder) must have a non-zero balance of BGLG tokens
Victim must have approved the attacker's address with allowance equal to uint256 max value (~uint256(0))

violation_target.exploit_hint: If a victim has approved your address with the maximum uint256 allowance (~uint256(0)), you can repeatedly call transferFrom to drain their entire token balance without the allowance being decremented. The check 'if (allowance[_from][msg.sender] < ~uint256(0))' will be false for max allowance, skipping the deduction. Call transferFrom multiple times with the victim's address as '_from' and your address as '_to', transferring their entire balance each time until it's depleted.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability exists in the transferFrom function where allowance deduction is skipped when allowance equals ~uint256(0) (max uint256). The condition 'if (allowance[_from][msg.sender] < ~uint256(0))' evaluates to false when allowance is exactly ~uint256(0), so the allowance is never reduced. This allows an attacker to repeatedly call transferFrom to drain the victim's entire token balance without the allowance being consumed.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Ensure the victim has a non-zero BGLG token balance. 2. Ensure the victim has approved the attacker with max allowance (~uint256(0)). 3. Repeatedly call transferFrom to transfer the victim's entire balance to the attacker until the victim's balance is depleted. 4. The allowance will never be reduced due to the bug, allowing unlimited transfers.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Set up the test environment with the target contract. 2. Identify a victim address with BGLG token balance. 3. Ensure the victim has approved the attacker with max allowance. 4. Call transferFrom multiple times to drain the victim's balance. 5. Verify the attacker's balance increased significantly.
